M_fixed: Let $N_3$ be the least $n$ such that there is $H=(H_1,\dots,H_n)$, each $H_i\in\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ homogeneous of degree 3, with $JH$ nilpotent (equivalently, for homogeneous $H$, $\det(I+JH)=1$) and $x+H$ not an automorphism of $\mathbb C^n$. Hubbers' classification of cubic homogeneous nilpotent Jacobians for $n\le4$ gives $N_3\ge5$ ($n=5$ is open as far as we know). De Bondt (arXiv:2610.24889, unrefereed), building on Alp\"oge's map and improving Van Rijn's 19, gives $N_3\le18$. Determine $N_3$; in particular, decide whether the Jacobian conjecture holds for cubic homogeneous maps in dimension 5. Companion: let $d_3$ be the least $\max_i\deg F_i$ over non-invertible Keller maps $F:\mathbb C^3\to\mathbb C^3$ ($\det JF\in\mathbb C^*$). Wang's theorem gives $d_3\ge3$ and Alp\"oge's map gives $d_3\le7$.
notes: Status checked. De Bondt 2610.24889 (Oct 2026, unrefereed, partly AI-written) gives HJC(18,3) via JC(12,3) and says Van Rijn reached 19. 18 is an 'absolute limit' only for that method. de Bondt-van den Essen 1609.09753 covers n<=4 and rk JH<=2; no HJC(5,3) proof found. Lower bound contains the classical open HJC(5,3). Upper bound may keep falling.

M_fixed: Let $d\ge1$, $a\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ be $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic with $\int_{[0,1]^d}a=0$, $a\not\equiv0$. Consider $u_t=\Delta u+a(x)u^p$, $u(\cdot,0)=u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R^d)$, $u_0\ge0$, $u_0\not\equiv0$. Prove: (i) if $1<p\le1+1/d$, every such solution blows up in finite time; (ii) if $p>1+1/d$, solutions with sufficiently small $u_0$ are global. Test case: $d=1$, $p=2$, $a=\cos(2\pi x)$ (equivalently $a=\cos x$ with $2\pi$-periodicity).
partial_result_check: The homogenization heuristic is correct. The corrector is $w=\phi v^p$ with $\Delta\phi=-a$, and averaging $p\,a\phi v^{2p-1}$ gives $c=\langle a,(-\Delta)^{-1}a\rangle>0$, so the threshold is $2p-1=1+2/d$, i.e. $p=1+1/d$. Other second-order terms ($\nabla\phi\cdot\nabla v^p$, $\phi\,\partial_t v^p$) give integrable mass. The original M is inconsistent: cos x is not Z-periodic.
notes: No literature on mean-zero periodic weights; Pinsky and Kawakami-Sire-Wang assume a>=0. But the near-identity change u=w+phi w^p seems to make (ii) routine: crude decay bounds on the new terms are integrable exactly when p>1+1/d. Subcritical blowup is plausibly within reach of test-function methods. Only the critical case looks hard. A nice but likely-routine niche Fujita variant, so B.

M_fixed: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a strictly convex body whose boundary is a real-analytic closed curve with curvature vanishing at at least one point (hence, by analyticity, at finitely many). For $p\in\mathbb R^2\setminus K$, let $T(p)=2q-p$, where $q\in\partial K$ is the tangency point of the tangent line from $p$ that has $K$ on its left. Is every $T$-orbit bounded, for every such $K$? If not, characterize the $K$ with unbounded orbits, e.g. by the vanishing orders of the curvature or by symmetry. First test case: $K=\{x^4+y^4\le1\}$.
partial_result_check: I checked the singularity claim. At a flat point of order k the radius of curvature satisfies rho(theta)~|theta|^{-k/(k+1)} (|theta|^{-2/3} for x^4+y^4), and the tangency point q(p) is only C^{1/(k+1)} across the tangent lines at the flat points. So T and the limiting map at infinity are genuinely non-smooth, and KAM does not apply directly. The claim is correct.
notes: Not found solved. Sorrentino 2610.06418 is C^1-generic and centrally symmetric only (the why should say so) and never mentions analytic tables or flat points. Dolgopyat-Fayad, Amiran, Boyland, and 2508.15142 all assume positive curvature or deal with corners or segments. A natural intermediate case for Moser's question.
